 Judgment

The appellants have filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC and have placed on record a certificate issued by the Sub-Registrar, Kalaburagi regarding the market value of the land in Kapnoor village.
He contends that the acquired land is very close to Kapnoor village which is used for non-agricultural purposes.
He has also placed on record a Google map, which indicates the distance between Tawargera and Kapnoor village.
He submits that these documents are relevant to establish that the land in question can be used for non-agricultural purposes.

He submits that these documents could not be produced before the Reference Court and therefore, prays NC:
2023:KHC-K:1089 that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Reference Court be set aside and the case be remitted back to the Reference Court for re-consideration.

2. The appellants are land losers who have filed this appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge at Kalaburagi (henceforth referred as 'Reference Court'), in LAC No.108/2009, vide judgment and award dated 30.04.2014.

sentences.text: 3. The appellants were the owners of the land bearing Sy.No.59/2 of Tawargera village, Kalaburagi Taluk and District measuring 2 acres 25 guntas, which was proposed for acquisition for formation of road between Tawargera to Harsur-Hebbal, in terms of a notification dated 09.03.2006 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the LA Act, 1894').
This notification was followed by a final notification dated 22.07.2007 published in the official gazette dated 23.08.2007.
Later an award passed on 15.04.2008 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1089 determining a sum of Rs.37,500/- per acre, treating it as an irrigated land.
The appellants dissatisfied by the award, sought enhancement which was referred under Section 18 of the LA Act, 1894.

The Reference Court registered it as LAC No.108/2009 and in terms of its judgment and award dated 30.04.2014 enhanced the compensation to a sum of Rs.3,05,370/- per acre along with all statutory benefits and interest.
4.
The appellants being not satisfied by the compensation enhanced by the Reference Court have filed this appeal.

The learned counsel for the appellants submits that the land in question lies very Neelkanth S/O Anneppa vs The Chief Engineer, Knnl Ip on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161081163/
2 close to Kalaburagi City and is also very close to an Industrial area in Kapnoor and therefore, the Reference Court failed to consider the non-agricultural potential of the land.

sentences.text:
He contends that several warehouses are constructed in Tawaragera village and therefore, it must have been valued accordingly.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1089 5.

Learned counsel for the respondents submits the compensation awarded by the Reference Court is just and proper and there is no justification provided by the appellants for not producing these documents before the Reference Court.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants as well as the learned counsel for the respondents.
7. The appellants lost their land for the formation of the road by the respondents between Tawargera to Harsur-Hebbal road.

The Land Acquisition Officer awarded the compensation of Rs.37,500/-,
which is enhanced to a sum of Rs.3,05,370/- per acre for wet land.
However, the Reference Court held that the acquired land has no potential for non-agricultural use.

Since it is stated by the learned counsel for the appellants that the Tawargera village lies very close to Kalaburagi city and also very near to an industrial area in Kapnoor village, the possibility of the land being used for non-agricultural purpose cannot be NC: 2023:KHC-K:1089 ruled out and therefore, in order to assess the real market value of the land lost by the appellants, this Court considers it appropriate to grant an opportunity to the appellants/claimants to adduce further evidence to establish the market value of the acquired land.
Hence, I.A.No.1/2023 is allowed.

However, the appellants cannot get the advantage of interest if the compensation is enhanced for the period commencing from the date of filing this appeal till today, as the appellants failed to produced any material before the Reference Court to establish the non-agricultural potential, but claimed that the land is irrigated and fertile and that there is a bore-well and well where a 5 HP motor is installed which is serviced with electricity.
Now after nearly 9 years, an application is filed under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC to produce additional documentary evidence claiming that the land in question was potential for non- agricultural use.
In that view of the matter, this appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge, Kalaburagi dated 30.04.2014 in LAC No.108/2009 is set aside.

The Reference Court shall thereafter decide the reference in accordance with law within a period of six months from the date of appellants concluding their evidence.
The Court fee paid by the appellants shall be refunded in accordance with law.
